title: Love God “with all thine heart” — the Greek of the verse says “mind”, and the Gospels quote it in two further forms
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, names three things: heart, soul and might. Brenton’s Greek of the same verse has mind, soul and strength. Matthew quotes three (heart, soul, mind) and Mark four (heart, soul, mind, strength).
text: KJV Deuteronomy 6:5: “And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.” KJV Matthew 22:37: “Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.” KJV Mark 12:30: “thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength” Hebrew (WLC) Deuteronomy 6:5: בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֥ וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וּבְכָל־מְאֹדֶֽךָ [with all thy heart and with all thy soul and with all thy might]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Deuteronomy 6:5: ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου, καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου, καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς δυνάμεώς σου [out of all thy mind, and out of all thy soul, and out of all thy strength]. Greek New Testament (TISCH) Matthew 22:37: ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου [in all thy heart and in all thy soul and in all thy mind]. Mark 12:30: ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου [out of all thy heart and out of all thy soul and out of all thy mind and out of all thy strength]. The Textus Receptus text served has the same words in both verses. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/5/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/DEU06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/40/22/, https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/40/22/, https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/41/12/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/41/12/.
reasoning: Where the KJV and the Hebrew have “heart”, Brenton’s Greek has the word for mind (διανοίας), the same word Matthew and Mark use for “mind” beside a separate word for heart (καρδία). The commandment therefore stands in four forms in the texts quoted: heart, soul, might (KJV and Hebrew); mind, soul, strength (Brenton’s Greek); heart, soul, mind (Matthew); heart, soul, mind, strength (Mark).
scope: G applies at Deuteronomy 6:5, where the Greek word differs from the KJV’s. Matthew 22:37 and Mark 12:30 are context: the KJV follows the Greek New Testament there and no tag applies. The record compares wording. It does not say that the forms command different things, that “heart” and “mind” were distinct ideas to the first hearers, or which form the Gospel writers had before them. title: “And serve him” — the Greek of the verse says “him only shalt thou serve”, the form quoted in Matthew
summary: In Matthew, Jesus quotes as written “him only shalt thou serve”. The KJV of Deuteronomy 6:13, with the Hebrew, has “and serve him” without “only”. Brenton’s Greek of the verse has “him only”, and adds “and thou shalt cleave to him”.

The KJV of Deuteronomy 6:13 and the Hebrew quoted have no word for “only”. The Greek of 6:13 also has a clause about cleaving to him, which the KJV has at 10:20 and not at 6:13.

title: The passover: “thou shalt roast and eat it” — the Greek says “boil and roast”, and the Hebrew verb is the one Exodus forbids with water
summary: Exodus forbids eating the passover “sodden at all with water” and requires it “roast with fire”. The KJV of Deuteronomy 16:7 says “roast”. The Hebrew verb there is the one rendered “sodden” in Exodus, not the Exodus word for roast, and Brenton’s Greek has two verbs: “thou shalt boil and roast”.
text: KJV Deuteronomy 16:7: “And thou shalt roast and eat it in the place which the Lord thy God shall choose” KJV Exodus 12:8: “they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire” KJV Exodus 12:9: “Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire” KJV 2 Chronicles 35:13: “And they roasted the passover with fire according to the ordinance: but the other holy offerings sod they in pots” Hebrew (WLC) Deuteronomy 16:7: וּבִשַּׁלְתָּ֙ וְאָ֣כַלְתָּ֔ [and thou shalt cook and eat]. Exodus 12:9: וּבָשֵׁ֥ל מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל בַּמָּ֑יִם כִּ֣י אִם־צְלִי־אֵ֔שׁ [nor cooked, cooked in water, but roast of fire]. 2 Chronicles 35:13: וַֽיְבַשְּׁל֥וּ הַפֶּ֛סַח בָּאֵ֖שׁ [and they cooked the passover in the fire]; וְהַקֳּדָשִׁ֣ים בִּשְּׁל֗וּ בַּסִּירֹ֤ות [and the holy things they cooked in the pots]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Deuteronomy 16:7: Καὶ ἑψήσεις καὶ ὀπτήσεις καὶ φαγῇ [and thou shalt boil and thou shalt roast and thou shalt eat]. Exodus 12:9: οὐδὲ ἡψημένον ἐν ὕδατι, ἀλλʼ ἢ ὀπτὰ πυρὶ [nor boiled in water, but only roast with fire]. 2 Chronicles 35:13: Καὶ ὤπτησαν τὸ φασὲκ ἐν πυρὶ [and they roasted the passover in fire]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/5/16/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/2/12/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/35/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/DEU16.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EXO12.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH35.htm.
reasoning: In Exodus 12:9 the Hebrew sets two words against each other: a verb of cooking, said there to be “in water”, which the KJV renders “sodden”, and a word for roasting. Deuteronomy 16:7 uses the first verb, with no mention of water or fire, and the KJV renders it “roast”. Brenton’s Greek of Deuteronomy 16:7 has both the verb it uses for the forbidden boiling in Exodus and the verb for roasting.
scope: G applies at Deuteronomy 16:7: the Greek names two acts where the KJV names one. No H is proposed. The Hebrew verb of Deuteronomy 16:7 is used with “in the fire” at 2 Chronicles 35:13, where the KJV again has “roasted”, and with “in water” at Exodus 12:9; it may therefore be a general word for cooking, and the KJV’s “roast” may be a fair rendering of it here. On that reading Deuteronomy does not conflict with Exodus. If the verb is read as boiling, the two instructions differ. The verse does not say which. A published record on the place of the passover leaves the cooking terms as a separate question; this record sets out the wording only. title: “Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people” — the Greek of the verse adds “let all the angels of God worship him”, the words quoted in Hebrews
summary: Hebrews 1:6 quotes “And let all the angels of God worship him”. Those words are not in the KJV or the Hebrew of Deuteronomy 32:43. They stand word for word in Brenton’s Greek of that verse, which has four calls to rejoice or worship where the KJV has one.

title: “From his right hand went a fiery law for them” — the Greek says “on his right hand were angels with him”
summary: The KJV says the Lord came “with ten thousands of saints” and that a fiery law went from his right hand. Brenton’s Greek has “with ten thousands of Kades” and, in place of the fiery law, angels at his right hand.

title: Moses: “he buried him” — the Greek says “they buried him”
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, says of Moses “he buried him”, with one burier who is not named in the verse. Brenton’s Greek has a plural: “they buried him”.
text: KJV Deuteronomy 34:5: “So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.” KJV 34:6: “And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.” Hebrew (WLC) 34:6: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ר אֹתֹ֤ו בַגַּיְ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מֹואָ֔ב מ֖וּל בֵּ֣ית פְּעֹ֑ור [and he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab over against Beth-peor]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 34:6: Καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν ἐν Γαὶ ἐγγὺς οἴκου Φογώρ [and they buried him in Gai near the house of Phogor].
